# Node64 – Models

<!-- Generated by Scripts/generate_docs.py – do not edit by hand. -->

Response models are `Codable, Hashable, Sendable` structs with `let` properties.
Most properties are optional because the API spec marks almost nothing as required – unwrap them.
Types conforming to `IPv64OpenEnum` are string-backed structs: compare with the listed constants,
use a `default` branch in `switch`, and create unknown values with `Type(rawValue:)`.
Input types (`…Input`) have a public memberwise `init` with `nil` defaults for optional fields.

## `Node64` (class)

Client for the local JSON API of a Node64 node in your own network.

- `configuration: Configuration` – The configuration this client was created with.

## `Node64.ACMEAuthority` (struct)

An additional ACME authority besides Let's Encrypt.

- `id: Int` – Authority ID.
- `name: String?` – Name.
- `directory: String?` – ACME directory URL.
- `eab: Bool?` – Requires External Account Binding.
- `eabKID: String?` – EAB key ID.
- `customRoot: Bool?` – Uses a custom root certificate.
- `certificates: Int?` – Number of certificates issued by it.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.

## `Node64.APIKey` (struct)

An API key of the signed-in user. The key itself is never returned after creation.

- `id: Int` – Numeric key ID.
- `name: String?` – Name of the key.
- `hint: String?` – Short hint (the last characters) to recognize the key.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `lastUsedAt: Date?` – Time of the last request made with this key.

## `Node64.AuditEntry` (struct)

An entry of the audit log.

- `id: Int` – Numeric entry ID (use as `before` cursor).
- `time: Date?` – Time of the action.
- `actor: String?` – Who performed the action.
- `action: String?` – Action name.
- `target: String?` – Object the action applied to.
- `details: String?` – Additional details.
- `ip: String?` – IP address of the caller.
- `origin: String?` – Origin: `local` (UI), `api:<key name> (<hint>)` or `peer` (other node of the group).

## `Node64.BackupRestoreResult` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Node/restoreBackup(_:password:)`.

- `restarting: Bool?` – The node restarts now.
- `bytes: Int?` – Database: size in bytes. Archive: number of files.

## `Node64.CDNAccessAction` (open enum)

Action of an access rule.

- `.allow` = `"allow"`
- `.deny` = `"deny"`

## `Node64.CDNAccessAuth` (open enum)

Forward-auth login service of an access list (`auth`).

- `.users` = `""`

- `.oauth2Proxy` = `"oauth2-proxy"`

## `Node64.CDNAccessForward` (struct)

Settings of the login service for forward auth (`forward` of `CDNAccessListInput`).

- `address: String?` – Check address, e.g. `http://authentik-server:9000/outpost.goauthentik.io/auth/traefik`.
- `headers: [String]?` – Response headers that go to the target.
- `callback: String?` – Path of the return route on the host.

## `Node64.CDNAccessList` (struct)

An access list (without passwords). Schema `CDNAccessList`.

- `id: Int` – Access list ID.
- `name: String?` – Name of the list.
- `satisfyAny: Bool?` – Either a user or an IP rule is enough.
- `passAuth: Bool?` – Pass the authorization header on to the target.
- `users: [CDNAccessListUser]?` – Users of the list.
- `rules: [CDNAccessRule]?` – IP rules of the list.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `updatedAt: Date?` – Time of the last update.
- `addKey: String?` – The new access key, only in the answer to a create or update with `CDNAccessListInput/addKey`. It is shown once; treat it as a secret. Not in the spec's response schema.

## `Node64.CDNAccessListEntry` (struct)

Entry of the access list overview: a list and the hosts using it.

- `accessList: CDNAccessList?` – The access list.
- `usedBy: [String]?` – Hosts that use the list.

## `Node64.CDNAccessListInput` (struct)

Writable fields of an access list. Schema `CDNAccessListInput`.

- `name: String?` – Name of the list.
- `satisfyAny: Bool?` – Either a user or an IP rule is enough.
- `passAuth: Bool?` – Pass the authorization header on to the target.
- `users: [CDNAccessListUserInput]?` – Replaces the users; `nil` = unchanged.
- `rules: [CDNAccessRule]?` – IP rules of the list.
- `loginPage: Bool?` – Sign in on a login page instead of the browser dialog.
- `auth: CDNAccessAuth?` – Login service (forward auth); `""` = users of the list.
- `forward: CDNAccessForward?` – Settings of the login service.
- `passUser: Bool?` – Pass Remote-User, -Email, -Groups and -Name on to the target.
- `addKey: String?` – Name of a new access key. The node returns the key once in `Node64/CDNAccessList/addKey`.
- `removeKeys: [String]?` – Access keys to delete (start of the key or hint).

## `Node64.CDNAccessListUser` (struct)

A user of an access list (without password).

- `username: String?` – User name.

## `Node64.CDNAccessListUserInput` (struct)

A user of an access list when writing; an empty password keeps the existing one.

- `username: String?` – User name.
- `password: String?` – Empty = keep the existing password.

## `Node64.CDNAccessRule` (struct)

An IP rule of an access list.

- `action: CDNAccessAction?` – Allow or deny matching addresses.
- `cidr: String?` – IP, network or `all`.

## `Node64.CDNAdvanced` (struct)

Advanced settings of a proxy host. Schema `CDNAdvanced`.

- `requestHeaders: [CDNHeader]?` – Headers added to the request.
- `requestRemove: [String]?` – Request headers to remove.
- `responseHeaders: [CDNHeader]?` – Headers added to the response.
- `responseRemove: [String]?` – Response headers to remove.
- `hostHeader: String?`
- `timeoutSeconds: Int?` – Timeout towards the target in seconds.
- `maxBodyMB: Int?` – Maximum request body size in MB.
- `noBuffering: Bool?` – Disable response buffering.
- `gzip: Bool?` – Compress responses with gzip.
- `trustedProxies: [String]?` – Trusted proxy addresses or networks.
- `accessLog: Bool?` – Write an access log.
- `noLimits: Bool?` – Disables the per-IP request limit and per-target limit (connection limits and bans still apply).
- `noProbe: Bool?` – Do not check the target for reachability (proxy hosts, TLS passthrough), e.g. for services without a web UI: no "unreachable" display, no `node64_cdn64_host_target_up` metric.
- `geoMode: CDNGeoMode?` – Country filter mode.
- `geoCountries: [String]?` – ISO country codes, at most 60 (e.g. `["DE", "AT"]`).
- `aiBots: Bool?` – Reject AI bots (403) by user agent. Proxy, redirect and status hosts only.
- `aiBotsAllowUser: Bool?` – Let requests made on behalf of a user pass the AI bot filter.
- `aiRobots: Bool?` – Serve a `/robots.txt` disallowing all AI bots when the target has none. Proxy hosts only.
- `bwDownMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth to the visitor (download) in Mbit/s for all requests of the host together; `0` = unlimited, 0-100000.
- `bwUpMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth from the visitor (upload) in Mbit/s; `0` = unlimited, 0-100000.
- `errorHTML: String?` – Own error page (proxy hosts only) instead of the neutral page for 502/503/504 of PROXY64, at most 64 KB.
- `errorOverride: Bool?` – Also replace 5xx answers of the target by `errorHTML` (the status code stays).
- `maintenance: Bool?` – Maintenance mode (proxy hosts only): maintenance page (503) instead of the target.
- `maintenanceHTML: String?` – Own HTML for style `custom`, at most 64 KB.
- `maintenanceStyle: CDNMaintenanceStyle?` – Maintenance page style, default `matrix`.
- `onlyLocations: Bool?` – Proxy hosts only: answer only the locations, all other paths 404 (needs at least one location).
- `targetPath: String?` – Proxy hosts only: path put before every request (`/recipes`: `/soup` becomes `/recipes/soup` at the target).
- `targetHTTP: ProxyTargetHTTP?` – Proxy hosts only: HTTP version towards the target; `""`/`auto` = automatic, `h1` = HTTP/1.1 only, `h2c` = HTTP/2 without TLS (gRPC) or HTTP/2 only for https targets. WebSocket upgrades always use HTTP/1.1; unknown values are rejected (400).
- `proxyProtocol: ProxyProtocolVersion?` – Kind `passthrough` only: PROXY protocol header to the target (sent before the ClientHello, also via CDN64); `""` = off. Only enable if the target expects it. Dropped for other kinds, unknown values are rejected (422).

## `Node64.CDNBlocklist` (struct)

One ipv64 blocklist.

- `id: String?` – ID from `https://ipv64.net/blocklists/index.json`, e.g. `all`, `spamhaus_drop`, `tor_exit`.
- `name: String?` – Name of the list.
- `category: String?`
- `text: String?` – Description from ipv64.net (English).
- `license: String?` – License of the list.
- `source: String?` – Project page of the source.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the list is enabled.
- `entries: Int?` – Number of loaded networks.
- `updated: Date?` – Last checked.
- `changed: Date?` – Last changed.
- `error: String?` – Error message of the last load.
- `edition: CDNBlocklistEdition?` – Honeypot category only: loaded edition.
- `liveDenied: Bool?` – The list token was not authorized; the daily snapshot was loaded.
- `liveError: String?` – Why the live fetch failed; never contains the token.

## `Node64.CDNBlocklistAIBots` (struct)

State of the AI bot user-agent list.

- `needed: Bool?` – An enabled host uses the list (it is only loaded then).
- `entries: Int?` – Number of loaded entries.
- `users: Int?` – Entries for requests made on behalf of a user.
- `updated: Date?` – Last checked.
- `changed: Date?` – Last changed.
- `error: String?` – Error message of the last load.
- `blocked: Int?` – Rejected since the start.

## `Node64.CDNBlocklistCountry` (struct)

Country list loaded for the country filter.

- `code: String?` – ISO country code.
- `entries: Int?` – Number of loaded networks.
- `updated: Date?` – Last checked.
- `error: String?` – Error message of the last load.

## `Node64.CDNBlocklistEdition` (open enum)

Edition of a honeypot blocklist.

- `.live` = `"live"`
- `.daily` = `"daily"`

## `Node64.CDNBlocklists` (struct)

State of the ipv64 blocklists. Schema `CDNBlocklists`.

- `lists: [CDNBlocklist]?` – The ipv64 blocklists.
- `allow: [String]?` – Exceptions: IP addresses or networks.
- `deny: [String]?` – Own deny list: IP addresses or networks rejected for all hosts and streams (the allow list wins).
- `denied: Int?` – Rejected by the own deny list since the start.
- `blocked: Int?` – Rejected since the start.
- `active: Bool?` – At least one list is loaded and enabled.
- `countries: [CDNBlocklistCountry]?` – Country lists used by the country filter.
- `geoBlocked: Int?` – Rejected by the country filter since the start.
- `tokenSet: Bool?` – A list token for the live edition is stored (never returned).
- `aiBots: CDNBlocklistAIBots?` – State of the AI bot user-agent list.

## `Node64.CDNGeoMode` (open enum)

Country filter mode (`geo_mode`) of hosts and streams.

- `.off` = `""`
- `.block` = `"block"`
- `.allow` = `"allow"`

## `Node64.CDNHeader` (struct)

A header name/value pair.

- `name: String?` – Header name.
- `value: String?` – Header value.

## `Node64.CDNHoneypotBlock` (struct)

A blocked IP of the honeypot.

- `ip: String?` – Blocked IP address.
- `reason: String?` – Why the IP was blocked.
- `since: Date?` – Blocked since.
- `until: Date?` – Blocked until.

## `Node64.CDNHoneypotRoute` (struct)

Which rejections go to the honeypot (`route` of `CDNHoneypotSettings`). Missing = default (everything except `geo`).

- `blocklist: Bool?` – Rejections by the blocklists.
- `honeypot: Bool?` – Rejections of IPs the honeypot reported.
- `exploit: Bool?` – Rejections of exploit attempts.
- `aiBot: Bool?` – Rejections of AI bots.
- `geo: Bool?` – Rejections by the country filter.

## `Node64.CDNHoneypotSettings` (struct)

Honeypot64 settings. Schema `CDNHoneypotSettings`.

- `route: CDNHoneypotRoute?` – Which rejections are handed to the honeypot.
- `decoy: Bool?` – Send requests without a matching host to the Honeypot64 web decoy.
- `access: Bool?` – Send access metadata to the Honeypot64 log sensor.
- `block: Bool?` – Block IPs reported by the honeypot locally right away.
- `blockHours: Int?` – Block duration in hours, 1-720 (default 24).

## `Node64.CDNHoneypotView` (struct)

Honeypot64 settings, blocked IPs and counters. Schema `CDNHoneypotView`.

- `settings: CDNHoneypotSettings?` – Honeypot64 settings.
- `decoyAvailable: Bool?` – Honeypot64 currently offers a web decoy.
- `accessAvailable: Bool?` – Honeypot64 currently evaluates accesses.
- `blocks: [CDNHoneypotBlock]?` – Currently blocked IPs.
- `rejected: Int?` – Rejected since the start.
- `decoyed: Int?` – Handed to the decoy since the start.
- `reported: Int?` – Handed to the log sensor since the start.

## `Node64.CDNHostWatch` (struct)

A health check that watches the target of a host. Schema `CDNHostWatch`.

- `token: String?` – Token of the health check.
- `name: String?` – Name of the health check.
- `type: String?` – Type of the health check.
- `state: String?`
- `paused: Bool?` – Whether the check is paused.
- `local: Bool?` – Runs on this node (not on ipv64.net or another node).
- `hostOnly: Bool?` – Ping: only the host matches.
- `lastCheck: Date?` – Time of the last check.

## `Node64.CDNJA4Mode` (open enum)

JA4 handling of CDN64 (`off`, `count`, `block`).

- `.unset` = `""`
- `.off` = `"off"`
- `.count` = `"count"`
- `.block` = `"block"`

## `Node64.CDNLimitBan` (struct)

A banned address.

- `ip: String?` – IPv4 address or IPv6 /64.
- `until: Date?` – Ban lifted at.

## `Node64.CDNLimits` (struct)

Overload protection settings per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64; `0` switches a limit off. Schema `CDNLimits`.

- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether overload protection is enabled.
- `connsPerIP: Int?` – Simultaneous connections per IP (default 200).
- `connRate: Int?` – New connections per IP and second, briefly ten times that (default 20).
- `reqRate: Int?` – Requests per IP and second, above that 429 (default 50).
- `reqBurst: Int?` – Requests in a row (default 500, at least `reqRate`).
- `maxConns: Int?` – Open connections overall (default 10000).
- `targetConns: Int?` – Simultaneous requests per proxy host to its target; others wait up to 10 s, then 503 (default 200).
- `banAfter: Int?` – Rejections within a minute before an IP is banned (default 300).
- `banMinutes: Int?` – Ban duration in minutes, at most 10080 (default 10).
- `exemptLAN: Bool?` – Never limit private addresses (default true).

## `Node64.CDNLimitsView` (struct)

Overload protection: settings, defaults, bans and counters. Schema `CDNLimitsView`.

- `limits: CDNLimits?` – Current limits.
- `defaults: CDNLimits?` – Default limits.
- `bans: [CDNLimitBan]?` – Currently banned addresses.
- `rejected: Int?` – Rejected since the start.
- `conns: Int?` – Currently counted open connections.

## `Node64.CDNLocation` (struct)

A path-specific target of a proxy host. Schema `CDNLocation`.

- `path: String?` – Path prefix.
- `scheme: ProxyHostScheme?` – Scheme of the target.
- `targetHost: String?` – Target name or IP.
- `targetPort: Int?` – Target port.
- `forwardPath: String?` – Replaces the path at the target.
- `websockets: Bool?` – Whether WebSockets are passed.
- `accessListID: Int?` – Access list ID; `0` = same as the host.
- `action: CDNLocationAction?` – What happens with the path: `""` = forward to the target (default), `block` = error page, `respond` = fixed answer.
- `status: Int?`
- `body: String?`
- `contentType: String?`
- `advanced: CDNLocationAdvanced?` – Own values of the location (action `""` only); unset values come from the host.
- `deniedRedirect: String?` – On denied access (access list answers 403): 302 redirect here instead of the error page; relative path (`/...`) or http(s) URL, `""` = error page. Not for lists that require a login (401).

## `Node64.CDNLocationAction` (open enum)

What a location does with its path (`action` of `CDNLocation`).

- `.forward` = `""`
- `.block` = `"block"`
- `.respond` = `"respond"`

## `Node64.CDNLocationAdvanced` (struct)

Own advanced values of a location (`advanced` of `CDNLocation`); unset values come from the host.

- `timeoutSeconds: Int?` – Timeout until the target answers in seconds; `0` = like the host.
- `maxBodyMB: Int?` – Maximum request body in MB; `0` = like the host, `-1` = unlimited.
- `buffering: CDNLocationBuffering?` – Buffering; `""` = like the host.
- `requestHeaders: [CDNHeader]?` – Headers added to the request.
- `requestRemove: [String]?` – Request headers to remove.
- `responseHeaders: [CDNHeader]?` – Headers added to the response.
- `responseRemove: [String]?` – Response headers to remove.
- `targetHTTP: ProxyTargetHTTP?` – HTTP version towards the target of this location; `""` = like the host.

## `Node64.CDNLocationBuffering` (open enum)

Buffering of a location (`buffering` of `CDNLocationAdvanced`).

- `.inherit` = `""`
- `.on` = `"on"`
- `.off` = `"off"`

## `Node64.CDNMaintenanceStyle` (open enum)

Maintenance page style (`maintenance_style` of `CDNAdvanced`).

- `.matrix` = `"matrix"`
- `.gear` = `"gear"`
- `.custom` = `"custom"`

## `Node64.CDNOnlineEdge` (struct)

## `Node64.CertDNSCheck` (struct)

Own resolvers of the DNS-01 check. Schema of `GET /certs/dns-check`.

## `Node64.CertDNSCheckPath` (struct)

One way the DNS-01 check can take.

- `name: String?` – Name of the way.
- `direct: Bool?` – Directly via the ipv64 name servers (otherwise a public resolver).
- `ok: Bool?` – The way works.
- `detail: String?` – Details.

## `Node64.CertDNSCheckResult` (struct)

Result of the DNS-01 check. Schema of `POST /certs/dns-check/run`.

- `paths: [CertDNSCheckPath]?` – All tested ways.
- `directOK: Bool?` – A direct way works.
- `publicOK: Bool?` – A public resolver works.
- `ok: Bool?` – At least one way works (one is enough).

## `Node64.Certificate` (struct)

A certificate without its private key.

- `id: Int` – Certificate ID.
- `names: [String]?` – DNS names and IP addresses.
- `source: CertificateSource?` – How the certificate is issued.
- `aliasZone: String?` – Alias zone (source `alias`).
- `aliasPrefix: String?` – Alias prefix (source `alias`).
- `staging: Bool?` – Issued by the Let's Encrypt test environment.
- `autoRenew: Bool?` – Renews automatically.
- `status: CertificateStatus?` – Issuing state.
- `step: String?` – Running step while the certificate is being fetched.
- `issuer: String?` – Issuer.
- `notBefore: Date?` – Start of validity.
- `notAfter: Date?` – End of validity.
- `lastError: String?` – Last error message.
- `lastAttempt: Date?` – Time of the last issuing attempt.
- `usedBy: [String]?` – Parts that use the certificate.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `updatedAt: Date?` – Last change.
- `dnsAccount: Int?` – DNS account (source `dns`).
- `caID: Int?` – Own CA (source `ca`).
- `days: Int?` – Validity in days (sources `ca`, `self`).

Result of `Node64/Certificates/bundle(_:format:ifNoneMatch:)`.

## `Node64.CertificateCreateInput` (struct)

Body of `Node64/Certificates/create(_:)`.

- `names: [String]` – DNS names or IP addresses.
- `source: CertificateSource` – How to issue the certificate.
- `aliasZone: String?` – Alias zone (source `alias`).
- `aliasPrefix: String?` – Alias prefix (source `alias`).
- `staging: Bool?` – Use the Let's Encrypt test environment.
- `autoRenew: Bool?` – Renew automatically (default on).
- `dnsAccount: Int?` – DNS account (source `dns`).
- `caID: Int?` – Own CA (source `ca`).
- `days: Int?` – Validity in days (sources `ca`, `self`); default 397, at most 825.
- `acmeCA: Int?` – Further ACME authority instead of Let's Encrypt (`0`).
- `keyType: CertificateKeyType?` – Key type for source `self` and the Let's Encrypt sources `ipv64`, `alias`, `http`, `dns`: ECDSA P-256 or RSA 2048 (e.g. for older devices like DSM 6); otherwise ignored. Default ECDSA.

## `Node64.Check` (struct)

A healthcheck as the node returns it. Schema `Check`.

- `token: String` – 32-character primary key.
- `name: String?` – Name of the check.
- `type: CheckType?` – Check type.
- `target: String?` – Target; depends on the type (URL, host, domain, empty for push).
- `params: [String: JSONValue]?` – Type-dependent parameters (method, headers, port, expect, `period_seconds`, …).
- `intervalSeconds: Int?` – Check interval in seconds (5 to 86400 locally, 20 to 86400 online/hybrid).
- `retryIntervalSeconds: Int?` – Interval in seconds while retrying after a failure.
- `retries: Int?` – Retries before the check counts as down (0 to 10).
- `connectTimeoutSeconds: Double?` – Connect timeout in seconds.
- `timeoutSeconds: Double?` – Timeout in seconds.
- `invert: Bool?` – Inverts the result.
- `stabilize: Int?` – Number of equal results needed to change state (1 to 20).
- `ipMode: CheckIPMode?` – IP version.
- `tags: [String]?` – Tags.
- `description: String?` – Free-form description.
- `paused: Bool?` – The check is paused.
- `parent: String?` – Token of the parent check.
- `critical: Bool?` – Marks the check as critical.
- `execution: CheckExecution?` – Where the check is measured.
- `policy: CheckPolicy?` – Overall state with several measuring points.
- `locations: [String]?` – Online locations (`nbg`, `fsn`).
- `notifyDegraded: Bool?` – Also notify when partly down.
- `notifyDown: Bool?` – Notify when down.
- `notifyUp: Bool?` – Notify when up again.
- `channels: [Int]?` – Notification channel IDs; empty means the default channels.
- `repeatMinutes: Int?` – Reminder interval in minutes during an outage (0 = off, up to 1440).
- `revision: Int?` – Revision counter (read-only).
- `createdAt: String?` – Creation time (read-only).
- `updatedAt: String?` – Time of the last change (read-only).
- `pushURL: String?` – Heartbeat URL of a push check (read-only).
- `state: CheckState?` – Current state (read-only).
- `group: String?` – Free-form group name (at most 100 characters).
- `nodes: [String]?` – IDs of the measuring nodes.
- `owner: CheckOwner?` – Which node owns the check (read-only).
- `id: String`

## `Node64.CheckInput` (struct)

Writable fields of a check, the body of create and update calls.

- `params: [String: JSONValue]?` – Type-dependent parameters.
- `intervalSeconds: Int?` – Check interval in seconds.
- `retryIntervalSeconds: Int?` – Interval in seconds while retrying (5 to `intervalSeconds`).
- `retries: Int?` – Retries before the check counts as down (0 to 10).
- `connectTimeoutSeconds: Double?` – Connect timeout in seconds.
- `timeoutSeconds: Double?` – Timeout in seconds.
- `invert: Bool?` – Inverts the result.
- `stabilize: Int?` – Number of equal results needed to change state (1 to 20).

- `repeatMinutes: Int?` – Reminder interval in minutes (0 to 1440).
- `group: String?` – Free-form group name (at most 100 characters).

## `Node64.DNS64DHCPScope` (struct)

A DHCP network (one per interface). Schema `DNS64DHCPScope`.

- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the network is on (read-only).
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time (read-only).

- `days: [Int]` – Weekdays, 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.
- `start: String` – Start time, e.g. `21:00`.
- `end: String` – End time, e.g. `07:00`.
- `action: DNS64ScheduleAction` – What the schedule does.
- `label: String?` – Label.
- `categories: [DNS64GroupCategory]?` – Categories blocked when `action` is `cats`.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the schedule is active.

## `Node64.DNS64Service` (struct)

A service that can be blocked per click. Entry of `DNS64Services/services`.

- `key: String?` – Key to pass in `categories` of a group rule or schedule, e.g. `svc:tiktok`.
- `id: String` – Service ID.
- `name: String?` – Display name.
- `group: String?` – Group of the service, e.g. `social`.
- `domains: [String]?` – Domains the service uses.

## `Node64.DNS64Services` (struct)

Categories and services a group can block, result of `Node64/DNS64/services()`.

- `categories: [String]?` – Category names.
- `groups: [String]?` – Service groups, e.g. `ai`, `social`, `messenger`.
- `services: [DNS64Service]?` – Services; block one with its `key` in `categories`.

## `Node64.DNS64Settings` (struct)

Settings of the DNS64 resolver. Schema `DNS64Settings`.

- `port: Int?` – DNS port.
- `bind: String?` – Bind address.
- `router: String?` – DNS server for local names.
- `retentionDays: Int?` – Days the query log is kept.
- `upstreamMode: DNS64UpstreamMode?` – How upstream servers are used.
- `upstreams: [DNS64Upstream]?` – Upstream servers.
- `lists: [DNS64List]?` – Blocklists.
- `allowLists: [DNS64List]?` – Allow lists: domains that no blocklist blocks (the own deny list takes precedence).
- `listHours: Int?` – Hours between blocklist updates.
- `blockMode: DNS64BlockMode?` – Answer for blocked domains.
- `cacheSize: Int?` – Maximum number of cache entries.
- `anonymize: DNS64Anonymization?` – Log anonymization.
- `allowNets: [String]?` – Networks allowed to use the resolver.
- `doh: Bool?` – DNS over HTTPS enabled.
- `dot: Bool?` – DNS over TLS enabled.
- `doq: Bool?` – DNS over QUIC enabled.
- `dohPort: Int?` – DoH port (443).
- `dotPort: Int?` – DoT (TCP) and DoQ (UDP) port (853).
- `names: [String]?` – Names of the node for devices and the certificate.
- `certMode: DNS64CertMode?` – Certificate source.
- `notifyUpstream: Bool?` – Notify when an upstream fails.
- `notifyLists: Bool?` – Notify when a blocklist fails.
- `acmeDomain: String?` – ACME: ipv64 domain.
- `acmePrefix: String?` – ACME: prefix.
- `acmeEmail: String?` – ACME: e-mail address.
- `acmeStaging: Bool?` – ACME: use the staging environment.
- `upstreamCount: Int?`
- `certID: Int?`
- `firefoxCanary: Bool?` – Answer `use-application-dns.net` with NXDOMAIN so Firefox disables its own DoH (default on).
- `mdns: Bool?` – mDNS bridge enabled (answers local names via multicast DNS).
- `docker: Bool?` – Docker integration enabled (entries from `node64.dns.name` container labels).
- `dockerIP: String?` – IP address used for Docker entries.

## `Node64.DNS64SettingsInput` (struct)

Changes for `Node64/DNS64/updateSettings(_:)`. Only fields you set are sent.

- `port: Int?` – DNS port.
- `bind: String?` – Bind address.
- `router: String?` – DNS server for local names.
- `retentionDays: Int?` – Days the query log is kept.
- `upstreamMode: DNS64UpstreamMode?` – How upstream servers are used.
- `upstreams: [DNS64Upstream]?` – Replaces the whole upstream list. Read it with `Node64/DNS64/settings()`, modify it and send the complete list back.
- `lists: [DNS64List]?` – Replaces the whole blocklist list. Read it with `Node64/DNS64/settings()`, modify it and send the complete list back.
- `allowLists: [DNS64List]?` – Replaces the whole allow list list. Read it with `Node64/DNS64/settings()`, modify it and send the complete list back.
- `listHours: Int?` – Hours between blocklist updates.
- `blockMode: DNS64BlockMode?` – Answer for blocked domains.
- `cacheSize: Int?` – Maximum number of cache entries.
- `anonymize: DNS64Anonymization?` – Log anonymization.
- `allowNets: [String]?` – Networks allowed to use the resolver.
- `doh: Bool?` – DNS over HTTPS enabled.
- `dot: Bool?` – DNS over TLS enabled.
- `doq: Bool?` – DNS over QUIC enabled.
- `dohPort: Int?` – DoH port (443).
- `dotPort: Int?` – DoT (TCP) and DoQ (UDP) port (853).
- `names: [String]?` – Names of the node for devices and the certificate.
- `certMode: DNS64CertMode?` – Certificate source.
- `notifyUpstream: Bool?` – Notify when an upstream fails.
- `notifyLists: Bool?` – Notify when a blocklist fails.
- `acmeDomain: String?` – ACME: ipv64 domain.
- `acmePrefix: String?` – ACME: prefix.
- `acmeEmail: String?` – ACME: e-mail address.
- `acmeStaging: Bool?` – ACME: use the staging environment.
- `upstreamCount: Int?`
- `certID: Int?`
- `firefoxCanary: Bool?` – Answer `use-application-dns.net` with NXDOMAIN so Firefox disables its own DoH (default on).
- `mdns: Bool?` – mDNS bridge enabled (answers local names via multicast DNS).
- `docker: Bool?` – Docker integration enabled (entries from `node64.dns.name` container labels).
- `dockerIP: String?` – IP address used for Docker entries.

Sort direction of a list.

- `.ascending` = `"asc"`
- `.descending` = `"desc"`

## `Node64.DNS64Status` (struct)

State of the DNS service, result of `Node64/DNS64/status()`.

- `version: String?` – Software version.
- `listen: String?` – Listen address (`address:port`).
- `startedAt: Date?` – Start time of the DNS service.
- `router: String?` – DNS server for local names (empty = none).
- `routerSource: String?` – Where `router` comes from: `config` or `auto`.
- `retentionDays: Int?` – Days the query log is kept.

## `Node64.DNS64Summary` (struct)

Key figures of a time range. Schema `DNS64Summary`.

- `summary: DNS64SummaryTotals?` – Counters of the requested range.
- `blocklistSize: Int?` – Number of blocklist rules loaded.
- `listsLoadedAt: Date?` – When the blocklists were loaded.
- `cache: DNS64Cache?` – Cache counters.
- `uptimeSeconds: Int?` – Seconds since the DNS service started.
- `version: String?` – Software version.

## `Node64.DNS64SummaryTotals` (struct)

Counters of a time range, nested in `DNS64Summary`.

- `total: Int?` – All queries.
- `blocked: Int?` – Blocked queries.
- `cached: Int?` – Queries answered from the cache.
- `clients: Int?` – Distinct clients.
- `avgUpstreamMs: Double?` – Average upstream response time in milliseconds.
- `droppedLogEntries: Int?` – Log entries dropped because the log queue was full.

## `Node64.DNS64Timeline` (struct)

Queries over time, result of `Node64/DNS64/timeline(range:)`.

- `stepMs: Int?` – Bar width in milliseconds (1h: 2 min, 24h: 30 min, 7d: 4 h).
- `buckets: [DNS64TimelineBucket]?` – The bars.

## `Node64.DNS64TimelineBucket` (struct)

One bar of `DNS64Timeline`.

- `t: Int?` – Start of the bucket as Unix time in milliseconds.
- `total: Int?` – Queries in the bucket.
- `blocked: Int?` – Blocked queries in the bucket.
- `date: Date?` – Start of the bucket as a date.

## `Node64.DNS64TopItem` (struct)

Entry of a top list. Schema `DNS64TopItem`.

- `count: Int?` – Number of queries.
- `blocked: Int?` – Number of blocked queries (client lists).
- `id: String` – Identifier for `Identifiable` (the name).

## `Node64.DNS64TopKind` (open enum)

Kind of a top list.

- `.clients` = `"clients"`

## `Node64.DNS64TopPage` (struct)

A page of the full top list, result of `Node64/DNS64/topList(kind:range:query:sort:direction:limit:offset:)`.

Sort field of `Node64/DNS64/topList(kind:range:query:sort:direction:limit:offset:)`.

An upstream server entry of the settings. Schema `DNS64Upstream`.

How several upstream servers are used.

## `Node64.DNS64Upstreams` (struct)

Upstream servers and the router for local names, result of `Node64/DNS64/Upstreams/list()`.

- `servers: [DNS64UpstreamStats]?` – Servers with statistics.

## `Node64.DNS64UpstreamStats` (struct)

An upstream server with statistics. Schema `DNS64UpstreamStats`.

- `name: String?` – Display name.
- `url: String?` – Server URL.
- `proto: DNS64Protocol?` – Transport: `doh`, `dot` or `doq`.
- `ips: [String]?` – Bootstrap IP addresses.
- `requests: Int?` – Number of requests sent.
- `wins: Int?` – Number of times it answered first.
- `errors: Int?` – Number of errors.
- `avgMs: Double?` – Average response time in milliseconds.

- `lastError: String?` – Last error message.
- `lastErrorAt: Date?` – Time of the last error.
- `active: Bool?`
- `pausedUntil: Date?` – The server is skipped until this time after repeated failures.

## `Node64.DNS64Zone` (struct)

Local DNS zone. Schema `DNS64Zone`.

- `id: Int` – ID of the zone.
- `name: String` – Zone name; a network like `192.168.1.0/24` becomes a reverse zone.
- `authoritative: Bool?` – Unknown names answer NXDOMAIN (otherwise they go on to forwards/router).
- `devices: Bool?` – Devices of the groups with a label are published as `<name>.<zone>`.
- `comment: String?` – Comment.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the zone is on.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `ttl: Int?` – Default TTL of new records (default 300).
- `refresh: Int?` – SOA refresh (default 3600).
- `retry: Int?` – SOA retry (default 600).
- `expire: Int?` – SOA expire (default 86400).
- `minimum: Int?` – TTL for "does not exist" (default 60).
- `hostmaster: String?` – SOA mail; empty means `hostmaster.<zone>`.
- `dynamic: Bool?` – Dynamic updates (RFC 2136) are on (read-only).
- `tsigName: String?` – TSIG key name (read-only).

## `Node64.DNS64ZoneInput` (struct)

Writable fields of a local zone. The on/off state is changed with enable/disable.

- `name: String` – Zone name or network.
- `authoritative: Bool?` – Unknown names answer NXDOMAIN.
- `devices: Bool?` – Publish device labels as `<name>.<zone>`.
- `comment: String?` – Comment.
- `ttl: Int?` – Default TTL of new records.
- `refresh: Int?` – SOA refresh.
- `retry: Int?` – SOA retry.
- `expire: Int?` – SOA expire.
- `minimum: Int?` – TTL for "does not exist".
- `hostmaster: String?` – SOA mail.

## `Node64.DNS64ZoneTSIG` (struct)

Key for dynamic updates (TSIG) of a zone. **Contains secret key material.**

- `zone: String?` – Name of the zone.
- `dynamic: Bool?` – Whether dynamic updates are on.
- `algorithm: String?` – Algorithm, e.g. `hmac-sha256`.
- `tsigName: String?` – Key name.
- `tsigSecret: String?` – Key (Base64). Secret: shown only by these endpoints, never in lists, exports or the cluster. Do not log it.

## `Node64.DNSAccount` (struct)

Credentials of a DNS provider for DNS-01 validation, without secret values.

- `providerName: String?` – Display name of the provider.
- `values: [String: String]?` – Non-secret fields; secret fields appear only as `"set"`.

- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.

One input field of a DNS provider.

- `optional: Bool?` – Field may stay empty.

## `Node64.EdgeConfig` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Honeypot/certificate(_:)` (202, issuing continues in the background).

## `Node64.Honeypot64Config` (struct)

Settings of the Honeypot64 sensor. Schema `Honeypot64Config`.

- `profile: Honeypot64Profile?` – Profile (default `standard`).
- `services: [Honeypot64ServiceConfig]?` – Services; only used with profile `custom`.
- `scan: Bool?` – Port scan detection (default `true`).
- `maxConnsPerIP: Int?` – Concurrent connections per source IP (0 = default 8, max 1000).
- `maxConnsTotal: Int?` – Concurrent connections in total (0 = default 512, max 100000).
- `retentionDays: Int?` – Retention in days (1-90, default 7).
- `maxEvents: Int?` – Maximum stored events (1000-5000000, default 200000).
- `notifyNew: Bool?` – At most one bundled message per hour for new source IPs (default `false`).
- `report: Bool?` – Report to ipv64 (opt-in; needs the central ipv64 API key, otherwise 400 with `fields.report`).
- `noLocalBlock: Bool?`
- `country: String?` – Location of the sensor (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2); empty = automatic.
- `log: Honeypot64LogConfig?` – Log sensor and syslog receiver.
- `certID: Int?` – Certificate of the certificate management for decoy names (0 or missing = off).
- `certPorts: [Int]?` – Ports that show the certificate despite a self-signed profile.
- `login: Honeypot64LoginConfig?` – Monitoring of the node's own login.

## `Node64.Monitor64AccessConfig` (struct)

Configuration of an access without secrets. It is checked strictly (unknown fields and fields of another access type give `400`). SNMP fields only for `snmp`, `metrics` only for `prom`. The same type is used in responses and requests; `nil` fields are not sent.

- `port: Int?` – Port (0 = default of the access type).
- `user: String?` – User (SSH and agent `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,32}$`; SNMPv3 at most 32 characters; otherwise up to 128 characters, also user@domain).
- `smart: Bool?` – SSH: SMART via sudo smartctl.
- `url: String?` – Address of the interface (at most 512 characters): http(s)://; Docker also unix://, tcp://, ssh://; TrueNAS and Redfish https:// only; NUT host[:3493] or nut://; Prometheus URL of the exporter; not allowed for SNMP.
- `tokenID: String?` – Token ID (e.g. Proxmox `user@realm!token`).
- `node: String?` – Node name (Proxmox VE).
- `pin: String?` – Certificate fingerprint (SHA-256 hex) or SSH host key (`SHA256:...`, Docker ssh://).
- `ups: String?` – NUT: UPS names, comma separated (empty = all).
- `tls: Monitor64AccessConfigTls?` – NUT: TLS mode.
- `api: Monitor64AccessConfigApi?` – TrueNAS: API flavour.
- `session: Bool?` – Redfish: session instead of basic auth.
- `mode: Monitor64AccessConfigMode?` – Agent: pull or push.
- `token: String?` – Agent in push mode: pointer to the access (at most 64 characters). Gives no access, so it is part of the response, but treat it like a secret.
- `metrics: [Metric]?` – Prometheus only: own metrics (at most 50).
- `snmpVersion: Monitor64AccessConfigSnmpVersion?` – SNMP: version.
- `level: Monitor64AccessConfigLevel?` – SNMPv3 level.
- `authProto: Monitor64AccessConfigAuthProto?` – SNMPv3 authentication.
- `privProto: Monitor64AccessConfigPrivProto?` – SNMPv3 encryption.
- `context: String?` – SNMPv3 context (usually empty).
- `custom: [CustomOID]?` – SNMP: own OIDs.
- `profiles: [String]?` – SNMP: fixed profiles (at most 16; empty = automatic).
- `traps: Bool?` – SNMP: accept traps of this host.
- `trapEngineID: String?` – SNMPv3: engine ID of the sender for traps (hex).

## `Node64.Monitor64AccessConfig.CustomOID` (struct)

A custom SNMP OID.

- `oid: String` – OID.
- `name: String` – Name.
- `unit: String?` – Unit.
- `factor: Double?` – Factor (0 = 1).
- `counter: Bool?` – Counter: rate per second times factor.
- `rule: String?` – Rule kind for thresholds, e.g. `temp.system`.

## `Node64.Monitor64AccessConfig.Metric` (struct)

A custom Prometheus metric.

- `name: String` – Metric name, e.g. `nginx_connections_active`.
- `labels: [String: String]?` – Labels that must match exactly (`""` = label missing or empty).
- `title: String?` – Display name (empty = name).
- `unit: String?` – Unit, e.g. `%`, `B`, `B/s`, `°C`, `ms`.
- `factor: Double?` – Value times factor (0 = 1).
- `rate: Bool?` – Counter: change per second.

## `Node64.Monitor64AccessInput` (struct)

Create or change an access. `secret` and `clearSecret` are write-only secrets: they are never returned (only `secretSet` on the response) and should not be logged.

- `type: Monitor64AccessType?` – Access type; required when creating, empty on PUT = unchanged.
- `config: Monitor64AccessConfig?` – Configuration. On PUT `nil` keeps the existing one (it is checked again).
- `secret: String?` – SECRET, write-only. Token or password; Docker: TLS key, certificate and CA as PEM or the private SSH key; SNMP: JSON `{"community", "auth", "priv"}` or just the community (empty fields keep the stored value). At most 4096 bytes, Docker 64 KiB. `nil`/empty = unchanged.
- `clearSecret: Bool?` – Remove the stored secret (write-only).
- `newToken: Bool?` – Agent in push mode: generate a new token.
- `hostkey: String?` – Confirmed SSH host key fingerprint (`SHA256:...`, taken while none is remembered); on PUT `reset` discards the remembered key.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Switch the access on or off; `nil` = unchanged (new: on).

## `Node64.Monitor64AccessState` (struct)

Access on the host page with runtime state: all fields of `Monitor64Access` plus state.

- `uid: String` – UID of the access.
- `type: Monitor64AccessType?` – Access type.
- `config: Monitor64AccessConfig?` – Configuration.
- `hostkey: String?` – Remembered SSH host key.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Switched on.
- `secretSet: Bool?` – A secret is stored (never returned).
- `name: String?` – Display name of the access type.
- `ok: Bool?` – Last query succeeded.
- `failures: Int?` – Failures in a row.
- `error: String?` – Error.
- `known: Bool?` – Already queried.
- `agent: Monitor64AgentHost?` – Agent state (agent accesses only).

Acknowledgement.

- `by: Monitor64Actor?` – Who acknowledged.
- `at: Date?` – When.
- `comment: String?` – Comment.

- `method: String?` – Sign-in method of people (currently always `local`).
- `ip: String?` – Address of the caller.

- `case offerAgain` – Offer as new again (`0`).

## `Node64.Monitor64HostCreate` (struct)

Creates a host with accesses (all fields on one level): the fields of `Monitor64HostInput` plus accesses and discovered services.

- `tags: [String]?` – Tags, lower-cased; duplicates and empty ones are dropped (at most 32).

- `paused: Bool?` – Pause queries.
- `agentAutoupdate: Bool?` – Update the agent automatically; `nil` = unchanged (new: on).
- `accesses: [Monitor64AccessInput]?` – Accesses (at most 8).
- `services: [Monitor64DiscoveredService]?` – Discovered services from the connection test (entered as new; at most 5000).
- `adopt: [String]?` – Keys of services to adopt immediately.

## `Node64.Monitor64Rule` (struct)

Rule of one level. Missing fields inherit field by field from the level below (default, deviation for group/tag, this host for all services of the kind, only this service). Number rules use `warn`/`crit` (or `warn_free`/`crit_free`), `dir`, `forSeconds`, `hyst` and `mode`; state rules use `severity` and `forSeconds`; `report` applies to both. Used as response and as input, `nil` fields are not sent.

- `warn: Monitor64Limit?` – Warning threshold (percent or value).
- `crit: Monitor64Limit?` – Critical threshold.
- `warnFree: Monitor64Limit?` – Warning in GB free (mode `free`).
- `critFree: Monitor64Limit?` – Critical in GB free (mode `free`).
- `dir: Monitor64RuleDir?` – Direction.
- `forSeconds: Int?` – Duration in seconds (0 to 31622400): all measurements in the period must be beyond the threshold.
- `hyst: Double?` – Hysteresis in units of the value (not negative).
- `mode: Monitor64RuleMode?` – Mode.
- `report: Monitor64RuleReport?` – Notify or only show.
- `severity: Monitor64RuleSeverity?` – Severity of a state rule.

- `kind: String?` – The kind.
- `group: String?`

- `factor: Double?` – Display value = value / factor.
- `store: Bool?` – Fill level: also "GB free".
- `state: Bool?` – State rule.
- `down: Bool?` – Threshold downwards.
- `nofor: Bool?` – Without duration.

- `warning: String?` – Warning.

## `Node64.ProxyHostInput` (struct)

Writable fields of a host. Schema `ProxyHostInput`.

- `kind: ProxyHostKind?` – Kind; only when creating, default `proxy`.
- `names: [String]?` – Domain names, also `*.domain`.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether it is enabled.
- `scheme: ProxyHostScheme?` – Scheme of the target.
- `targetHost: String?` – Target name or IP.
- `targetPort: Int?` – Target port.
- `websockets: Bool?` – Whether WebSockets are passed.
- `blockExploits: Bool?` – Block common exploit requests.
- `cacheAssets: Bool?` – Cache static assets.
- `certID: Int?`
- `forceSSL: Bool?` – Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
- `http2: Bool?` – Enable HTTP/2.
- `http3: Bool?` – Enable HTTP/3.
- `hsts: Bool?` – Send the HSTS header.
- `hstsSubdomains: Bool?` – Include subdomains in HSTS.
- `minTLS: ProxyHostMinTLS?` – Minimum TLS version.
- `verifyTarget: Bool?` – Verify the certificate of an https target (default off).
- `requestCertificate: ProxyHostCertificateRequest?` – Request a certificate for all domains in the background; a failure shows up as `certificateError`.
- `redirectTarget: String?` – Redirect target `domain[:port][/path]`.
- `redirectScheme: ProxyHostRedirectScheme?` – Scheme of the redirect target.
- `redirectCode: Int?` – One of 300, 301, 302, 303, 307, 308.
- `preservePath: Bool?` – Append the requested path to the redirect target.
- `accessListID: Int?`
- `locations: [CDNLocation]?` – Path-specific targets.
- `advanced: CDNAdvanced?` – Advanced settings.
- `createDNSRecord: ProxyHostDNSRecordRequest?` – Create a DNS record in the ipv64 account for every domain (existing ones stay).
- `statusPageID: Int?` – Status page ID (required, > 0, for kind `status`).

## `Node64.ProxyHostKind` (open enum)

Kind of a proxy host.

- `.tls13` = `"1.3"`

Reachability of the target of a host.

- `error: String?` – Error message of the last check.
- `checkedAt: Date?` – Time of the last check.
- `since: Date?` – Since when the state holds.

## `Node64.ProxyHostReachState` (open enum)

Reachability state of a target.

- `.unknown` = `"unknown"`
- `.up` = `"up"`
- `.slow` = `"slow"`
- `.down` = `"down"`

## `Node64.ProxyHostRedirectScheme` (open enum)

Scheme of a redirect target.

- `.auto` = `"auto"`
- `.http` = `"http"`

URL scheme of a proxy target (`http` or `https`).

- `.http` = `"http"`
- `.https` = `"https"`

## `Node64.ProxyHostStats` (struct)

Request counters of a host since the module started.

- `requests: Int?` – Requests since the module started.
- `errors: Int?` – Failed requests since the module started.
- `blocked: Int?` – Rejected requests since the module started.

## `Node64.ProxyProtocolVersion` (open enum)

PROXY protocol header sent to a target (`proxy_protocol`).

- `.off` = `""`

- `.v2` = `"v2"`

## `Node64.ProxyStream` (struct)

A TCP/UDP stream. Schema `Stream` (renamed, the name is too generic).

- `id: Int` – Stream ID.
- `name: String?` – Name of the stream.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the stream is enabled.
- `listenPort: Int?` – Port the stream listens on.
- `tcp: Bool?` – Whether TCP is served.
- `udp: Bool?` – Whether UDP is served.
- `targetHost: String?` – Target name or IP.
- `targetPort: Int?` – Target port.
- `tlsCertID: Int?` – TCP: terminate TLS with this certificate; `0` = raw.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `updatedAt: Date?` – Time of the last update.
- `running: Bool?` – Whether the stream is running.
- `reach: JSONValue?` – Reachability of the target (free-form object).
- `listenErrors: [String: String]?` – Why a port (`tcp`/`udp`) is not open.
- `stats: ProxyStreamStats?` – Connection counters.
- `certName: String?` – Name of the certificate used for TLS termination.
- `geoMode: CDNGeoMode?` – Country filter mode; changing it does not restart the stream.
- `geoCountries: [String]?` – ISO country codes, at most 60.
- `bwDownMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth to the visitor in Mbit/s for all connections together; `0` = unlimited.
- `bwUpMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth from the visitor in Mbit/s; `0` = unlimited.
- `proxyProtocol: ProxyProtocolVersion?` – TCP only: PROXY protocol header to the target (`""` = off); sent before all data, only enable if the target expects it. UDP-only streams answer 422; changing it does not restart the stream.

## `Node64.ProxyStreamInput` (struct)

Writable fields of a stream. Schema `StreamInput` (renamed).

- `name: String?` – Name of the stream.
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether it is enabled.
- `listenPort: Int?` – Port the stream listens on.
- `tcp: Bool?` – Whether TCP is served.
- `udp: Bool?` – Whether UDP is served.
- `targetHost: String?` – Target name or IP.
- `targetPort: Int?` – Target port.
- `tlsCertID: Int?` – TCP: terminate TLS with this certificate; `0` = raw.
- `geoMode: CDNGeoMode?` – Country filter mode.
- `geoCountries: [String]?` – ISO country codes, at most 60.
- `bwDownMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth to the visitor in Mbit/s for all connections together, 0-100000; `0` = unlimited.
- `bwUpMbit: Int?` – Bandwidth from the visitor in Mbit/s, 0-100000; `0` = unlimited.
- `onlineName: String?` – Port mapper: expose the port via CDN64 under this name (mode 3); `""` = local only.
- `proxyProtocol: ProxyProtocolVersion?` – TCP only: PROXY protocol header to the target (`""` = off); sent before all data, only enable if the target expects it. UDP-only streams answer 422; changing it does not restart the stream.

## `Node64.ProxyStreamStats` (struct)

Connection counters of a stream.

- `connections: Int?` – Total connections since the start.
- `active: Int?` – Currently active connections.
- `bytesIn: Int?` – Bytes received from clients.
- `bytesOut: Int?` – Bytes sent to clients.

## `Node64.ProxyTargetHTTP` (open enum)

HTTP version towards the target (`target_http`).

- `.inherit` = `""`
- `.auto` = `"auto"`
- `.h1` = `"h1"`
- `.h2c` = `"h2c"`

Answer of a push heartbeat (`{"status": "ok"}`).

- `status: String?`

## `Node64.PushStatus` (open enum)

Status reported by a push heartbeat (query `status`).

- `.up` = `"up"`
- `.down` = `"down"`

## `Node64.Sonar64Inbound` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Sonar64/inbound(since:)`.

- `ready: Bool?`
- `rows: [Sonar64InboundRow]?` – Measurements of this node by others (at most 500).

## `Node64.Sonar64InboundProbe` (struct)

A probe answered live in `Sonar64Recent`.

- `from: String?` – Short ID (8 hex characters) of the measuring node.
- `name: String?` – Name of the measuring node.
- `fam: Int?` – IP family (4 or 6).
- `count: Int?` – Number of probes.
- `at: Date?` – Time of the last probe.

## `Node64.Sonar64InboundRow` (struct)

A row of `Sonar64Inbound`.

- `from: String?` – ID of the measuring node.
- `name: String?` – Name of the measuring node.
- `asname: String?` – AS name.
- `place: String?` – Place.
- `trust: Sonar64TrustLevel?` – Trust level of the measuring node.
- `fam: Int?` – IP family (4 or 6).
- `method: String?` – Method.
- `avg: Double?` – Average round-trip time.
- `loss: Double?` – Loss as a fraction from 0 to 1.
- `at: Date?` – Time of the measurement.

## `Node64.Sonar64NodeState` (struct)

The `node` object of `Sonar64Status`.

- `nodeID: String?` – Node ID.
- `registered: Bool?` – The node is registered at ipv64.
- `mode: String?` – Mode.
- `measured: Bool?` – The node is measured too (UDP 6464 open).
- `budget: String?` – Budget.
- `responder: Bool?` – The node answers probes.
- `planIssued: Date?` – Issue time of the measurement plan.
- `planExpires: Date?` – Expiry of the measurement plan.
- `anchorsOnly: Bool?` – Only anchors are measured.
- `paused: Sonar64PauseReason?` – Why measuring is paused.
- `sentToday: Int?` – Probes sent today.
- `lastReport: Date?` – Time of the last report.
- `buffered: Int?` – Results waiting to be reported.
- `lastError: String?` – Last error.

## `Node64.Sonar64Recent` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Sonar64/recent(n:)`.

- `results: [Sonar64Result]?` – Own measurements, newest first.
- `inbound: [Sonar64InboundProbe]?` – Probes answered live on UDP 6464.
- `responder: Bool?` – The node answers probes.

## `Node64.Sonar64Result` (struct)

An own measurement in `Sonar64Recent`.

- `at: Date?` – Time of the measurement.

- `method: Sonar64Method?` – Method.
- `fam: Int?` – IP family (4 or 6).
- `sent: Int?` – Probes sent.
- `recv: Int?` – Probes received.
- `min: Double?` – Minimum round-trip time.
- `avg: Double?` – Average round-trip time.
- `max: Double?` – Maximum round-trip time.
- `loss: Double?` – Loss in percent.
- `err: String?` – Error.

## `Node64.Sonar64Settings` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Sonar64/settings()`.

- `participate: Bool?` – The node takes part.
- `measured: Bool?` – The node is measured too (UDP 6464).
- `budget: Sonar64Budget?` – Budget.
- `quiet: String?` – Quiet hours `from-to` in hours, e.g. `23-6`; empty = none.
- `name: String?` – Name of the node.
- `lat: Double?` – Latitude.
- `lon: Double?` – Longitude.
- `access: Sonar64Access?` – Connection type.
- `device: Sonar64Device?` – Device type.

Body of `Node64/Sonar64/updateSettings(_:)`. Omitted (`nil`) fields stay unchanged.

- `participate: Bool?` – Take part or leave.

- `budget: Sonar64Budget?` – Budget.
- `quiet: String?` – Quiet hours `from-to`, e.g. `23-6`.
- `name: String?` – Name of the node.
- `lat: Double?` – Latitude.
- `lon: Double?` – Longitude.
- `clearLocation: Bool?` – Delete the location.

- `device: Sonar64Device?` – Device type.

## `Node64.Sonar64Status` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Sonar64/status()`.

- `running: Bool?` – The module is running.
- `startedAt: Date?` – Start time.
- `keySet: Bool?` – A central ipv64 API key is stored.
- `participate: Bool?` – The node takes part in Sonar64.

- `publicURL: String?` – Public node page on ipv64.net.

## `Node64.Sonar64Trust` (struct)

The `trust` object of `Sonar64Status`.

- `level: Sonar64TrustLevel?` – Level.
- `next: String?` – Next level.
- `pct: Int?` – Progress to the next level in percent.
- `days: Int?` – Days of participation.
- `needDays: Int?` – Days needed for the next level.
- `uptime: Double?` – Uptime.
- `needUptime: Double?` – Uptime needed for the next level.
- `needMeasured: Bool?` – Being measured is needed for the next level.

## `Node64.StatusGroup` (struct)

Schema `StatusGroup`: a group of entries on a status page.

- `id: Int` – ID of the group (changes whenever the groups of the page are replaced).
- `name: String?` – Heading (up to 100 characters), empty for no heading.
- `items: [StatusItem]?` – Entries of the group.

## `Node64.StatusItem` (struct)

Schema `StatusItem`: an entry (check) of a group.

- `id: Int` – ID of the entry.
- `token: String` – Token of the check.
- `label: String?` – Display name (up to 120 characters); empty uses the check's name.

## `Node64.StatusNotice` (struct)

Schema `StatusNotice`: an announcement on a status page with its timeline.

- `id: Int` – ID of the notice.
- `pageID: Int?` – ID of the status page.
- `title: String?` – Title.
- `level: StatusNoticeLevel?` – Severity.
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `updatedAt: Date?` – Time of the last change.
- `resolvedAt: Date?` – Time it was marked resolved; absent while open.
- `updates: [StatusNoticeUpdate]?` – Timeline entries.

## `Node64.StatusNoticeInput` (struct)

Schema `StatusNoticeInput`: body for creating a notice.

- `title: String` – Title (up to 200 characters).
- `level: StatusNoticeLevel?` – Severity; the server defaults to `info`.
- `text: String?` – First timeline entry in simple Markdown (up to 5000 characters).

## `Node64.StatusNoticeLevel` (open enum)

Severity of a status page notice.

- `.info` = `"info"`
- `.warning` = `"warning"`
- `.danger` = `"danger"`
- `.unchanged` = `""`

## `Node64.StatusNoticeUpdate` (struct)

An entry in the timeline of a `StatusNotice`.

- `id: Int` – ID of the entry.
- `time: Date?` – Time of the entry.
- `text: String?` – Text in simple Markdown.

## `Node64.StatusNoticeUpdateInput` (struct)

Schema `StatusNoticeUpdateInput`: body for adding an update to a notice.

- `level: StatusNoticeLevel?` – New severity; `nil` or `StatusNoticeLevel/unchanged` keeps it.
- `text: String?` – Update text (up to 5000 characters); empty or `nil` adds none.
- `resolve: Bool?` – Mark the notice as resolved.

## `Node64.StatusPage` (struct)

Schema `StatusPage`: a public status page with groups of checks.

- `id: Int` – ID of the page.
- `slug: String?` – Slug in the URL `/status/<slug>`.
- `title: String` – Title (up to 120 characters).
- `description: String?` – Description in simple Markdown.
- `footer: String?` – Footer in simple Markdown.
- `enabled: Bool?`
- `publishNode: Bool?` – Serve the page directly on the node port under `/status/<slug>`.
- `layout: StatusPageLayout?` – Layout of the entries.
- `theme: StatusPageTheme?` – Color theme.
- `lang: StatusPageLanguage?` – Language (empty = language of the browser).
- `accent: String?` – Accent color as `#rrggbb`, empty for the default.
- `days: Int?` – Number of day bars (30, 60 or 90).
- `showUptime: Bool?` – Show uptime percentages.
- `showHistory: Bool?` – Show incidents and notices of the last 30 days.
- `refreshSec: Int?` – Refresh interval of the page in seconds (30 to 3600).
- `hasPassword: Bool?` – A password protects the page.
- `noindex: Bool?` – Ask search engines not to index the page.
- `poweredBy: Bool?` – Show "provided with Node64".
- `groups: [StatusGroup]?` – Groups with their entries (at most 50 groups and 1000 entries).
- `createdAt: Date?` – Creation time.
- `updatedAt: Date?` – Time of the last change.
- `hcGroups: Bool?` – Show entries in the healthcheck groups; the page's groups then only select and order.
- `hasLogo: Bool?` – A custom logo is uploaded.
- `logoUpdated: Date?` – Time of the last logo change (absent without logo).

## `Node64.StatusPageGroupInput` (struct)

A group to send when creating or replacing the groups of a status page.

- `name: String?` – Heading (up to 100 characters), empty for none.
- `items: [StatusPageItemInput]?` – Entries of the group.

## `Node64.StatusPageInput` (struct)

Writable fields of a status page for create (`POST`) and partial update (`PUT`).

- `slug: String?` – Slug; empty on create derives it from the title.
- `title: String?` – Title (required on create, up to 120 characters).
- `description: String?` – Description in simple Markdown (up to 5000 characters).
- `footer: String?` – Footer in simple Markdown (up to 2000 characters).
- `enabled: Bool?` – Whether the page is reachable.
- `publishNode: Bool?` – Serve the page directly on the node port.
- `layout: StatusPageLayout?` – Layout.
- `theme: StatusPageTheme?` – Color theme.
- `lang: StatusPageLanguage?` – Language.
- `accent: String?` – Accent color `#rrggbb`.
- `days: Int?` – Day bars: 30, 60 or 90.
- `showUptime: Bool?` – Show uptime percentages.
- `showHistory: Bool?` – Show incidents and notices of the last 30 days.
- `refreshSec: Int?` – Refresh interval in seconds (30 to 3600).
- `password: String?` – New password (4 to 72 characters); `"-"` removes it; `nil` or empty keeps it.
- `noindex: Bool?` – Ask search engines not to index the page.
- `poweredBy: Bool?` – Show "provided with Node64".
- `groups: [StatusPageGroupInput]?` – Replaces all groups and entries (their IDs change); `nil` keeps them.
- `hcGroups: Bool?` – Show entries in the healthcheck groups.

## `Node64.StatusPageItemInput` (struct)

An entry to send inside a `StatusPageGroupInput`.

- `token: String` – Token of the check.
- `label: String?` – Display name (up to 120 characters); empty uses the check's name.

## `Node64.StatusPageItemsInput` (struct)

Request body of `Node64/HC/StatusPages/addItems(_:_:)`.

- `groupID: Int?` – Group to add to (`0` or `nil` = the first group).
- `tokens: [String]?` – Check tokens.

## `Node64.StatusPageLanguage` (open enum)

Language of a status page.

- `.browser` = `""`
- `.de` = `"de"`
- `.en` = `"en"`

## `Node64.StatusPageLayout` (open enum)

Layout of a status page.

- `.list` = `"list"`
- `.tiles` = `"tiles"`
- `.compact` = `"compact"`

## `Node64.StatusPageTheme` (open enum)

Color theme of a status page.

- `.auto` = `"auto"`
- `.light` = `"light"`
- `.dark` = `"dark"`

## `Node64.StatusPageView` (struct)

What a status page shows right now (`GET /status-pages/{id}/view`), same structure as the page's `status.json`.

- `raw: JSONValue` – The complete JSON object.

## `Node64.Version` (struct)

Result of `Node64/Node/version()`.

- `version: String?` – Version of the node software.
- `startedAt: Date?` – Start time of the node process.
- `hostname: String?` – Host name of the node.
- `time: Date?` – Server time.

## `Node64APIError` (struct)

An error document returned by a Node64 node.

- `status: Int` – HTTP status code of the response (not part of the JSON body).
- `error: String?` – Error message, e.g. `invalid api key`.
- `field: String?` – Affected input field, if any.
- `fields: [String: String]?` – Messages per input field (validation errors).
- `code: String?` – Machine-readable code, e.g. `no_api_key`, `limit_reached` (PROXY64 online errors).
- `key: String?` – i18n key of the message, e.g. `hc.status.err.slug` (status page errors).
- `text: String?` – Localized error text with a hint how to fix it.
- `retryAfter: Int?` – Seconds to wait before retrying, from the `Retry-After` header (429).

## `Node64Error` (enum)

Errors thrown by `Node64`.

- `case api(Node64APIError)` – The node answered with an error document (`{"error": "…"}`).
- `case httpStatus(code: Int, body: Data)` – The node answered with an error status but no readable error document.
- `case missingAPIKey` – The endpoint requires an API key, but the client has none.
- `case invalidResponse` – The response was not an HTTP response.
- `case invalidRequest(String)` – The request URL could not be built from the given parameters.
- `case decoding(any Error, body: Data)` – The response body could not be decoded.
- `case encoding(any Error)` – A request body could not be encoded.
- `statusCode: Int?` – The HTTP status code, if the error came from the node.
- `code: String?` – The machine-readable code (e.g. `no_api_key`) or i18n key, if the node sent one.
- `errorDescription: String?`
